summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 5 upside misses — EL.PA +5%, DTG.DE +4%, BAB.L +3%, ADYEN.AS +3%, RNO.PA +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 3 downside moves (PUB.PA -5%, ABF.L -4%, ENGI.PA -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: PUB.PA (-4.95%) — Stock went ex-dividend on 2026-07-02 (€3.75/share, ~4.3% of prior close ≈86.46); the bulk of the -4.95% 'move' is a mechanical price adjustment, not a real selloff — no negative news/earnings/M&A found for the date. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe (in_universe_of empty) — PUB.PA is a French CAC40 large-cap advertising name; uk-eu strategies likely don't cover this sector/listing, and even if they did, ex-dividend gap days are typically excluded from momentum/gap scanners to avoid corporate-action noise.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear firm-specific news found for 2026-07-02; likely an oversold technical bounce after the stock's ~40% slide since its Nov 2025 peak, ahead of July 28 H1 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — EL.PA is a mega-cap (€86B) French CAC40/Euronext Paris consumer-healthcare crossover (eyewear/AI glasses) name that the uk-eu region universe apparently doesn't include, likely due to sector/listing-venue scoping rather than size.
top_movers.suggestion: Audit the uk-eu universe's inclusion rule for Euronext Paris large-caps in the consumer/healthcare crossover sector (e.g. CAC40 constituents) and add EL.PA if it's missing due to sector-tag mismatch rather than a deliberate exclusion.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a secondary sector tag for industrials with disclosed defense-revenue exposure (e.g. >5% of segment revenue or a named defense sub-brand) so defense-momentum strategies can include cross-listed names like DTG.DE alongside pure-play peers.

top_movers.catalyst: UK govt confirmed £15bn ($19.9bn) boost to Defence Investment Plan, lifting spend to 2.7% GDP by 2029 — sector-wide rally, Babcock +3.3%, BAE +2.0%, QinetiQ +2.4%

top_movers.suggestion: Add LSE defense primes (BAE, Babcock, QinetiQ, Rolls-Royce) to the uk-eu universe and add a policy-news scanner that flags sector-wide rallies off government spending announcements.

top_movers.catalyst: No single dated headline for 07-02; extends a multi-week re-rating on Adyen's €335M Orb acquisition (Jun), the Adyen Agentic AI-commerce launch, and JPMorgan's Positive Catalyst Watch call.
